paragraphs: Hey guys!
My name's Vikram. I'm a PhD student in Computer Science at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign.
Research Interests:
cards.research_short: I'm interested in "computation to help us understand us".
cards.research_long: The general theme I like to tie my diverse interests together with is the idea of "computation to help us understand us". There's a really common doctrine in behavioral science that says that our human behaviors have multiple levels of abstraction, from social to psychological to neurological (link). Under the mentorship of my PhD advisors (Prof. Bertram Ludäscher at UIUC and Prof. Jana Diesner at TUM), I am working on computational models to understand the diffusion of textual information in social networks. I'm also interested in using large language models (LLMs) as a tool to help us understand human cognition and creativity. Under the mentorship of Prof. Ramki Kannan and Ashish Gautam at ORNL, I am also working on a newfound interest of mine: neuromorphic computing, which is the design of computing systems inspired by the human brain. It's a particularly interesting way of using models of inference to understand our own neurological processes.

paragraphs: Hobbies and Miscellaneous

I enjoy longboarding. I love animals: I ride and take care of horses and have three cats (scroll to see them!). I'm passionate about languages (though I have varying proficiency in them): I speak English, Telugu, Japanese (~N4 level), and I learned Spanish in high school and college.
